answer.rationale: Constraints bind hard: 14 days to expiry, line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and one decision slot. That combination rules out a primary-vendor switch this cycle even though memory_c2 records a sharp unit-cost win from moving to the low-cost vendor — that record does not describe a 14-day cutover against a line with zero slack, and onboarding speed observed under slack conditions should not be assumed to transfer. add_second_source (memory_c3) addresses availability risk, not the 18% spend mandate, and would consume the cycle without touching cost. defer_decision (memory_c5) applied to a non-critical renewal; this contract is critical and does not auto-renew, so drifting past expiry risks uncovered supply. That leaves negotiate_terms, which is the only direction that attacks cost while leaving the integration and delivery schedule untouched (memory_c1). I am verifying memory_c4 because it is the load-bearing record for this choice: my plan rests specifically on its claim that market-rate benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, and I need the original to see how much margin was actually recovered and whether it was anywhere near 18% — if it was a few points, negotiation alone will not meet the mandate and the next review must sequence a switch or dual-source. memory_c6's multi-year volume pricing is a lever to pair with the negotiation, but I will not lock a long term this cycle: doing so would forfeit the option to move to the low-cost vendor once the line has buffer. Value risk to flag downstream: an 18% cut extracted purely on price can be quietly recovered by the vendor through narrowed service scope, expedite fees, or slower lead times — memory_c6 explicitly notes scope was preserved in that instance, so scope preservation is a term to write down, not assume. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose original context is archived, none carry the current volume or capacity conditions, and I am verifying only one, so the other five remain unaudited inferences.
